items.title: Amazonian animism meets the "Rights of Nature" at the RAI Myers Lecture
items.summary: Aparecida Vilaça of the Museu Nacional, Rio de Janeiro, gave this year's Myers Lecture at King's College London following the RAI AGM, where the 2026 RAI medals and awards were also announced.

items.title: Six senior promotions at UCL Anthropology
items.summary: Promotions recognise colleagues working across social, biological, environmental and evolutionary anthropology, from fiscal relations and the state to conservation and the evolution of human birth.

items.title: London Anthropology Day welcomes the next generation
items.summary: The annual taster day gives school students considering university a first experience of anthropology lectures, workshops and conversations with current students.

items.title: UCL alumna Myriam Lamrani shares the 2026 Edie Turner First Book Prize
items.summary: Lamrani's first book, The Intimacy of Images, has been co-awarded this year's Edie Turner First Book Prize.

items.title: Can South Asia's student uprisings build solidarity across borders?
items.summary: Durham political anthropologist Nayanika Mookherjee argues in The Wire and Bangladesh's New Age that youth protests share struggles over jobs, education, free expression and state power, and could link up despite regional tensions.

items.title: Georgina Born convenes an international summit on public service media
items.summary: The UCL anthropologist has organised an international summit on the future of public service media.

items.title: St Andrews opens virtual fellowships for scholars in Gaza
items.summary: The Department of Social Anthropology is offering three one-term Virtual Fellowships in 2026/27 for Palestinian scholars based in Gaza.

items.title: ERC funds Toby Kelly's study of private detectives
items.summary: Edinburgh anthropologist Professor Toby Kelly has won European Research Council funding for a study of private detectives.

items.title: ERC Advanced Grant for Christos Lynteris: Zoonosis Before Bacteriology
items.summary: The St Andrews anthropologist has won a European Research Council Advanced Grant for a project on understandings of zoonotic disease before bacteriology. In September he also received a BA/Leverhulme grant comparing French and British colonial maps of endemic disease.

items.title: Why more births now end in caesarean section
items.summary: Drawing on fieldwork in Bangladesh, Durham researcher Halima Akhter shows how fear, trust in doctors and worries about blame push caesarean rates up, and how much of the long recovery falls on families.

items.title: A ten-point manifesto for anthropology's future
items.summary: Anthropologists from industry, policy and academia met at UCL East to debate AI, the public good and how universities prepare anthropologists for work beyond academia. Contributors included Gillian Tett.

items.title: Why births have fallen to a fifty-year low
items.summary: Oxford anthropologist Dr Paula Shepard commented for the BBC on what lies behind the UK's falling birth rate and how people weigh the decision to have children.

items.title: The case for maintenance in a culture obsessed with change
items.summary: Durham anthropologists Tom Yarrow and Paolo Heywood use the work of stonemasons to argue that keeping things going is skilled, demanding labour that politics too often mistakes for doing nothing.

items.title: Solving the puzzle of human right-handedness
items.summary: Research by Thomas Püschel and Rachel Hurwitz (Oxford) with Chris Venditti (Reading) offers an evolutionary account of why most people favour their right hand.

items.title: Why do some people eat soil?
items.summary: Durham PhD researcher Zander Simpson traces geophagy from deep prehistory to prison diets and modern tasting menus, weighing up its cultural meanings and health risks.

items.title: Alpa Shah on the legacy of Jaipal Singh Munda
items.summary: Oxford's Professor of Social Anthropology writes in Outlook India on the Adivasi leader, Olympian and Constituent Assembly member, and what his politics mean today.

items.title: Oxford tops the 2026 QS ranking for anthropology
items.summary: The School of Anthropology and Museum Ethnography is ranked first in the world for the subject in this year's QS World University Rankings.

items.title: New podcast: Fieldnotes from Sussex Anthropology
items.summary: Hosted by Dr Syeda Sana Batool, the series ranges across trade, fieldwork, memory, therapy and AI in accessible conversations with Sussex anthropologists.
